$schema-note: v1.0.0-recovery-testing skip-enforcement manifest (design.md §1.1, Task 0.4). This is the AUTHORITATIVE required set: 'required' lists the stable id of EVERY non-live crash/soak test that MUST execute-and-pass in the required gate (G9). check-required-tests.ts fails the gate by id if any required id is missing or reported skipped/todo/failed. 'deferred' lists WHERE-gated optional-feature ids that reconcile as skipped-pending-feature and are exempt while their feature is unshipped. Each governed test embeds its id as a [[id]] token in its title (which Vitest surfaces in assertionResults[].title/fullName). The Task-0 crash-harness smoke ids (crash-harness.smoke.*) plus the full T1/T2/T5/T3/soak/load-under-prune/P3 id set below form the contract that Tasks 1-6 tag their tests with; the ids are defined NOW so later tasks adopt them verbatim without a spec rewrite. CHANGE-LEVEL AUDIT (BLOCK 9): check-required-tests.ts now FAILS CLOSED (a missing/unparseable/empty-or-absent required set fails the gate, never reconciles as 'all 0 passed'), STRUCTURALLY PINS required.length to EXPECTED_REQUIRED_COUNT (currently 65: the 25 v1.0.0-recovery-testing ids plus the 40 token-indexer / chain-archive-result ids added by project 00020, sub-plan 01 Phase 7) so silently deleting or adding a required entry fails the gate, and BINDS each required id to its 'file' so an id that executed-and-passed from a DIFFERENT file (a token moved to a trivial passing test) fails. The co-transactional saveAndAdvance crash test (crash.saveAndAdvance.co-tx-atomic, BLOCK 1) is required entry #23; the change-level round-3 differential negative-control (BLOCK 3) and reference import-clean (BLOCK 4) guards are required entries #24 and #25; every required entry MUST carry its bound 'file'.
$check-mechanism-note: IMPORTANT: run against the CURRENT Task-0-only suite, check-required-tests.ts will correctly report the not-yet-built required ids (the crash.* / soak.* / property.p3.* entries) as `missing` — those tests are authored by Tasks 1-6. That is EXPECTED and correct: check-required-tests.ts is the G9 RELEASE gate, green only once every task has landed its tagged tests. The check MECHANISM itself is proven independently, right now, by the synthetic-payload unit tests in check-required-tests.test.ts (which use an inline manifest, not this file), so those unit tests stay green regardless of how many required ids are still unbuilt. Do NOT delete a required id to make the check pass early — that would re-open the exact self-skip hole this manifest closes.

required.description: 0.1: spawn the crash worker, SIGKILL it, confirm the shared container is still up and a fresh client connects.
0.1: pg_terminate_backend drops a targeted backend's connection and the dedicated pool recovers (reconnects with a new backend pid).
0.3: a query against a deliberately-stalled backend is bounded by a 1.5s override of the suite watchdog and throws a typed SuiteWatchdogTimeoutError before G7's 120s, not a hang.
0.3: withSuiteWatchdog with NO explicit override applies SUITE_WATCHDOG_MS as its default bound (proven fast via fake timers, so the default is wired without a real 60s wait).
0.2: without UMBRADB_CRASH_HOOK the worker performs an ordinary uninterrupted save and exits 0.
0.2: the before-commit hook pauses after the manifest INSERT is issued, before COMMIT, and emits its readiness signal (incl. the worker backend pid); nothing is visible.
0.2: the in-critical-section hook pauses inside a held withLease; exactly one class-2 advisory lock with objid = hashtext(leaseKey) is held.
0.2: the after-data-commit-before-cursor hook runs TWO real ops (save then cursor) with a pause between; killed at the pause it leaves data durable and the cursor absent (watermark behind data).
0.2: the after-cursor-before-data hook runs TWO real ops (cursor then save) with a pause between; killed at the pause it leaves the cursor durable and the data absent (T5 unsafe reference case).

0.2 (test-honesty): the SAME co-transactional data->cursor flow run to completion WITHOUT a kill lands BOTH data and cursor — the negative control proving the killed T5 runs' absences are caused by the crash, not by a missing op.

T1 (Task 1.1): SIGKILL at before-commit leaves no complete=true manifest at the interrupted seq; the prior seq still loads+hash-verifies; no orphan junction rows; negative control (no kill => visible complete manifest).

T2 (Task 2.1): Postgres killed mid-save => the in-flight save rejects with a typed ConnectionError (not a raw driver error); after recovery the checkpoint is all-or-nothing and load(latest) returns correct bytes.

T2 (Task 2.2): the lost-COMMIT-ack state built by the sanctioned simulation (a provably-committed save re-invoked with identical content) yields a benign identical-content duplicate at the next seq; load(latest) correct either way; static check that save is excluded from any auto-retry allowlist.

T5 (Task 3.1, depends on G5): killed at after-data-commit-before-cursor, the durable watermark is never ahead of durable data (every write batch with cursor <= durable watermark is present in durable data).

T5 (Task 3.1, depends on G5): replay from the durable cursor converges on a current state equal (current-state equality predicate: kv_current + latest complete checkpoint payload + watermark values; excludes kv_history/version) to a fault-free in-repo reference replay of the same write-batch sequence.
T5 (Task 3.2, depends on G5): the watermark-never-ahead invariant holds under synchronous_commit = on.

T5 (Task 3.2, depends on G5): under synchronous_commit = off with an UNCLEAN postmaster kill (pg_ctl stop -m immediate / in-container kill -9), a lost tail of acknowledged commits is acceptable but an inverted durability order (cursor durable, data not) is a failure.
T3 (Task 4.1): after a lease-holder is SIGKILLed, a fresh process's withLease on the same key acquires immediately (bounded wait, no wedge) and pg_locks shows the class-2 advisory lock gone.

Soak (Task 5.1): a sustained concurrent mix at a declared envelope (10^5-10^6 chunks) samples a named P1-P10-derived SQL-observable invariant set DURING the run (gapless per-key version, only complete manifests loadable, no dangling junction, watermark <= max durable data); end state equals a fault-free reference; each GC-pass duration is recorded and bounded by GC_PASS_WATCHDOG_MS (no perf threshold gates).

Load-under-prune (Task 5.2): a FORCED, verified interleave lands the prune COMMIT inside load's open REPEATABLE READ snapshot window; load returns correct bytes and never raises ChunkIntegrityError/ChunkMissingError for a surviving checkpoint; negative control (un-snapshotted read of a reclaimed chunk DOES raise ChunkMissingError) fires.

P3 anchor (Task 6.1): the existing P3 replay/fold-equivalence property (getAt matches a from-scratch fold of the put sequence) is the differential gate's fold-equivalence anchor, satisfied WITHOUT importing the replaced store. Task 6.1 tags the existing P3 test with this id; no new test code.

Differential fault-schedule (Task 6.2, depends on G5): a SEEDED (reproducible, no Math.random) schedule mixing the G9 faults T1/T2/T5 across write batches, re-syncing from durable state after each fault, converges to a current state EQUAL (current-state predicate: full kv_current + full watermarks + latest complete checkpoint payload; excludes kv_history/version) to a fault-free in-repo reference run (a replay via UmbraDB's own adapters — NOT reference-merge.ts, which is transaction-history-merge only; no foreign consumer/indexer import, verified by an in-test import audit) of the same schedule. Mandatory negative control: a deliberately-broken variant that drops a committed range makes the equivalence assertion FIRE.

Co-transactional G5 crash (change-level audit BLOCK 1): saveAndAdvance — the single-transaction save+cursor combinator — SIGKILLed BETWEEN its internal checkpoint-data write and its cursor write (both inside the ONE uncommitted tx, paused via a test-only query observer over saveAndAdvance's own sql, NO src change) leaves NEITHER the checkpoint NOR the watermark advance durable (all-or-nothing), and a fresh saveAndAdvance on the same key then lands seq 1 committing both; a no-kill co-tx-full-flow control lands BOTH. Crash-tests G5 atomicity DIRECTLY (the two-transaction T5 tests never crash saveAndAdvance itself).

Differential negative control (change-level round-3 BLOCK 3): the mandatory dropped-range negative control - a deliberately-broken variant that skips one faulted batch's recovery so a committed range is genuinely dropped - makes the SAME current-state equality predicate the positive test relies on FIRE (throw). Required-enforced so deleting/skipping the control (or weakening assertCurrentStateEqual) turns the gate red by id.

Differential reference import-cleanliness (change-level round-3 BLOCK 4): a static audit that the in-repo reference imports nothing outside the repo - directly AND through its relative-import closure - catching bare import, dynamic import() and require(), and rejecting any @midnightntwrk/indexer/consumer/wallet specifier. Required-enforced so skipping/removing it turns the gate red by id.

00020 Phase 1 (spec §6.1, FR-008): the token_index lineage applies on a fresh database, is a no-op on re-run, and seeds exactly the two built-in rows — NIGHT (colour 32 zero bytes, 6 decimals) and DUST (colour NULL, domain_sep pad32("dust"), 15 decimals) — with the exact bytes, asserted against ledger-v9 itself (nativeToken().raw, and that no DUST colour exists) so the seeds cannot drift from the chain.

00020 Phase 1 (spec §6.1): every CHECK and key constraint of the token_index DDL is enforced by the database — byte lengths on address/domain_sep/color/payload, the kind/storage/status enumerations — and `rebuild` empties the tables and re-seeds the built-in rows.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §4.2 (SC-004): byte-exact parse of a 256-byte TokenMetadata payload at literal offsets (domainSep 0, kind 32, key 33, len 65, value 66), all four kind bytes, an empty and a full 190-byte value, and encode/decode round-tripping through the module's own encoder.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §4.2 (SC-004): one negative fixture per rejection rule — all 18 stable RejectReason tokens — each rejected with the expected reason and in the specified order; a rejected event is still fully decodable so it can be stored as evidence.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §4.2: the well-known key registry — name, symbol, decimals, metadata, metadata/<n> part indices, tokenUri — with their per-key validation (UTF-8, length bounds, decimals ≤ 36, absolute http(s) tokenUri) and the strict treatment of malformed keys (not UTF-8, interior NUL, malformed metadata part index).

00020 Phase 3 / spec §6.4 (SC-003): the derived colour persistentCommit([domainSep, address], pad32("midnight:derive_token")) reproduces all six colours RECORDED FROM LIVE STAGENET, each cross-checked against the published mint-test-tokens registry tokenId and, for the two unshielded issuers, against the tokenType of the UTXO the mint actually created.

00020 Phase 3 / spec §0, FR-008: NIGHT is 32 zero bytes by definition and is never derived — pinned against ledger-v9's nativeToken().raw — and the all-zero (address, domainSep) pair does NOT derive to it, which is exactly why NIGHT is seeded rather than derived.

00020 Phase 3: the colour helpers refuse malformed input instead of deriving a plausible wrong colour — non-32-byte arguments throw, the two arguments are not interchangeable, and the strict hex decoder throws where Buffer.from(s, "hex") would silently truncate at the first bad nibble.

00020 Phase 4 / spec §6.3, FR-001/FR-003 (SC-002): 12 REAL Stagenet transactions in a real chain_archive decode to exactly 6 contracts with their deploy heights, 6 observed/native token rows whose colour equals tokenColor(domainSep, address) and, for the unshielded issuers, the tokenType of the created UTXO, and 6 token_mints rows; a second scan writes nothing and reports atTip.

00020 Phase 4 / spec FR-002: a transaction whose archived result is `failure` yields a contract row but no token and no mint, and a non-canonical block is invisible to the scanner — nothing the ledger rejected ever becomes a token.

00020 Phase 4 / question Q33(b): a transaction whose archived `result` is NULL BLOCKS the decode cursor rather than being guessed at or skipped, and the scan proceeds unchanged once the result is backfilled — bounded by the UNKNOWN_RESULT_GRACE_MS grace so an unresolvable transaction cannot wedge the pipeline.

00020 Phase 4 / FR-014 (SC-005): a simulated crash mid-batch leaves contracts=0, mints=0, cursors=0 — rows and cursor are written in ONE database transaction — and a clean re-scan afterwards produces the full, identical result.

00020 Phase 6: the decode cursor walks over transaction-free blocks up to the archive's canonical tip (read BEFORE the batch that proves the range empty), so on a quiet chain /internal/status still shows the decoder keeping up instead of appearing stalled.

00020 Phase 4 / spec FR-002: the countedEffects rule exhaustively — a guaranteed-transcript mint counts on success and partial_success, a fallible mint counts only when its own intent segment succeeded, a segment absent from a PARTIAL_SUCCESS list counts as failed, and a partial_success transaction with no archived segments is an explicit error naming the transaction.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §6.5, FR-004: against a fake HTTP indexer, a short delivery queues the (contract, transaction) pair in pending_event_lookups while the scan cursor still advances, the drain completes it, and the end state is BYTE-EQUAL to a one-shot run; a duplicated delivery applies nothing new; paging by offset is exercised.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §6.5: more events returned than the transcript's log-op count is a HARD error (the model would be wrong) — it throws and leaves tokens=0, events=0, cursors=0, i.e. the batch is aborted rather than partially applied.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §6.5: a 503 mid-drain records attempts and the HTTP error on the pending row with exponential backoff, and a row that has exhausted its 30-attempt budget is skipped by the drain but KEPT and visible in /internal/status rather than retried forever or deleted.

00020 Phase 5 / spec FR-005: events that are not MiscContractEvent, and Misc events whose name is not pad32("TokenMetadata"), are counted against the log-op total but NEVER stored — only the standard's own events reach token_metadata_events.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §6.2, FR-007 (the status table row by row): observed (mint only), declared (event only), described (mint + agreeing event), inconsistent (event declaring ledger over an observed native mint) and builtin — recomputed from the stored evidence, never incremented.

00020 Phase 5 / spec FR-017(c), §7.1 row 12 (Ledger Liar): a declaration of kind byte 2 over an observed native mint sets status=inconsistent, keeps storage=native and the mint counters, still projects the declared fields, and STAYS inconsistent even after a later well-formed native declaration — the evidence is never erased.

00020 Phase 5 / FR-006: arrival order is irrelevant — mint-then-event and event-then-mint converge to the identical row, because status/storage/color are re-derived from stored evidence rather than accumulated.
00020 Phase 5 / spec Edge Cases, §7.1 row 10 (Dual Aurora): one colour with two kinds is TWO clean described rows keyed (net, address, domain_sep, kind), not one row and not an inconsistency.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §4.2 rule (b), FR-006: last write wins ordered by (block height, indexer event id) — including two events in one block — and a late-DELIVERED older event must not win; the superseded events stay in token_metadata_events as history.

00020 Phase 5 / spec FR-005 (SC-004): a rejected event is stored with applied=false and its reject_reason and changes NOTHING about the token row — the evidence is visible through the API while the table stays clean.

00020 Phase 5 / spec §4.2 metadata/<n>: split JSON projects only when parts 0..max are ALL present and the concatenation parses as a JSON object; a missing or invalidating part clears the projection to NULL while the parts themselves stay in token_metadata_kv.
00020 Phase 5 / FR-008, question Q30: the seeded NIGHT and DUST rows are untouched by the fold — no event and no mint can overwrite a builtin row.

00020 Phase 6 / spec §5 (FR-009): GET /v1/tokens over a REAL http server — the kind/storage/status filters, `q` by name prefix, symbol prefix and exact colour, and KEYSET pagination that walks every row exactly once (so a row inserted by the live scanner between two pages cannot make a reader skip or repeat a token).

00020 Phase 6 / spec §5: the per-token routes — the Token object, its key/value traits with full provenance (updatedHeight, updatedTxHash, eventId) and its mint history — with last-write-wins visible through the API.

00020 Phase 6 / spec §5, question Q51: the contract route, by-color, the raw events route ({ items, nextCursor }, ?applied=false, ?domainSep=) and GET /v1/registry.json keyed by colour for described native tokens.

00020 Phase 6 / spec §5 tokenUri resolver: /{token-name}/{id} answers identically in all three spellings (symbol, name slug, 64-hex) case-insensitively, 404s an unknown id, returns 409 TOKEN_AMBIGUOUS with candidates when two tokens share a symbol, and redirects an Accept: text/html request to the page's token view.

00020 Phase 6 / spec §5: the error contract — 400 TOKEN_BAD_REQUEST, 404 TOKEN_NOT_FOUND, 503 TOKEN_DB_UNAVAILABLE — plus the page routes (/ → 302 /ui, /ui → 200 with its CSP) and the resolver's matching helpers.

00020 master Phase C.1 (SC-004): all 69 payloads RECORDED FROM THE REAL COMPILED REFERENCE CONTRACTS (acedward/mip-erc7496-midnight-contracts, pinned in token-indexer/test/fixtures/contracts/SOURCE.md) parse byte for byte through the same parser the live indexer uses — the standard's bytes are pinned to an independent implementation, not to this repo's own encoder.

00020 master Phase C.1 (SC-004): the 7 negative payloads the reference contracts emit on purpose behave exactly as intended — including the one that is deliberately VALID (kind 0x03, shielded ledger) — so a rejection rule cannot quietly become a rejection of something legitimate.

00020 master Phase C.1 (SC-003): all 15 recorded colour vectors and all 16 recorded mint colours are reproduced by this repo's own derivation — the contract's tokenColor() circuit and the indexer agree on every byte.

00020 master Phase C.1: replaying the whole recorded corpus through the fold produces EXACTLY the 16 expected token rows across all four status values, including Ledger Liar collapsing onto ONE inconsistent row and Dual Aurora as two rows sharing one colour.

00020 Phase 2 / spec FR-002, question Q8: chain-archive-sync writes transactions.result and the new segments jsonb from the same block query, inside storeFetchedBlock and BEFORE the watermark advances, so a crash in between re-runs it; a re-ingest REPAIRS result, which the store's bare ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING cannot.

00020 Phase 2 / spec FR-002: the backfill-results command fills result/segments for blocks archived before this change by re-querying the indexer per block, is idempotent (UPDATE … WHERE result IS NULL), is safe against a live growing archive, and leaves system transactions' correct NULL alone.

00020 Phase 2 / question Q32: the additive chain_archive/002_tx_result_segments migration adds segments jsonb to the RANGE-partitioned parent (metadata-only, no rewrite) with its jsonb_typeof array CHECK, upgrades an existing archive in place by migration name, and is applied WITHOUT any edit under src/.

00020 Phase 2: mapTransactionResult maps SUCCESS|PARTIAL_SUCCESS|FAILURE to the archive's enum, returns undefined for "the source said nothing" (a system transaction) and THROWS on an unknown status rather than inventing one.

00020 sub-plan 03 / spec §8, US4 (SC-006): serveUi answers GET|HEAD /ui with 200, text/html and the page's hash-based CSP, redirects / to /ui, and returns false for every other path AND method without touching the response (proved by a Proxy that throws on any access); the served HTML contains no external resource URL.
